_about: The WWII pack's system pictures (tools/look/make_ww2_flags.py): each system flies a flag that identifies that country itself, never its conqueror's (TeeJ, 2026-09-30), and that a historian would accept for the war years: its own national flag (a government in exile's counts), else its own state's, national movement's or colony's flag of the war years; the flag of whoever held it only where it had none of its own then, or is part of that country (Sicily, Siberia). Germany flies the black-white-red tricolour: no Nazi symbols in the game at all (TeeJ, 2026-09-29). `flags`: the Wikimedia Commons file of each - its page, its SVG's address and SHA-1 as Commons publishes them, the PNG Commons renders from it (and that PNG's SHA-256), its licence; a flag with `parts` is those flags side by side. `systems`: which flag each system flies, and why.

germany.why: Germany's black-white-red tricolour, its national flag of 1933-35, in place of the swastika flag (TeeJ, 2026-09-29)

austria.why: Austria's own flag; annexed by Germany in 1938.

czechoslovakia.why: Czechoslovakia's own flag, flown by its government in exile in London.

gibraltar.why: A British colony since 1713, with no flag of its own until 1982.

poland.why: Poland's own flag, flown by its government in exile in London.

baltic_states.why: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, each its own flag of 1918-1940, side by side: the system is all three, annexed by the Soviet Union in 1940.

belarus.why: Belarus's own flag in the war years, the Byelorussian SSR's (1937-1951).

ukraine.why: Ukraine's own flag in the war years, the Ukrainian SSR's (1937-1949).

russia.why: The Soviet Union's own heart: Moscow was its capital.

caucasus.why: Three Soviet republics (Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan) and part of Soviet Russia, in one system.

kazakhstan.why: Kazakhstan's own flag in the war years, the Kazakh SSR's (1940-1953).

morocco.why: Morocco's own flag (1915), kept under the French protectorate.

algeria.why: Algeria's own flag: first sewn for Messali Hadj's Etoile Nord-Africaine in 1934, set in its present form by the Algerian People's Party in 1943-44.

tunisia.why: Tunisia's own flag, the beys' since 1831, kept under the French protectorate.

libya.why: The Senussi banner: the Senussi order led Libya's resistance to Italy, and its emir Idris sided with Britain in 1940; Cyrenaica's flag from 1949. Libya had no flag of its own until then.

malta.why: Malta's own white and red, with the George Cross the island was awarded in April 1942 for the siege, on a blue canton: used on the island from 1943, flown by Malta at the 1948 Olympics.

syria.why: Syria's own flag, the State of Syria's under the French mandate (1930-1958). Lebanon, in the same system, had its own from 1943.

palestine.why: The Palestine Mandate's own ensign (1927-1948), the only Palestine-specific flag not restricted to government use.

greenland.why: A Danish colony, with no flag of its own until 1985.

newfoundland.why: Newfoundland's own flag (1904-1949), with the Newfoundland seal.

alaska.why: The Territory of Alaska's own flag, adopted in 1927.

korea.why: Korea's own flag, the taegukgi, as the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea flew it in exile (Chongqing from 1940; at war with Japan from December 1941). Korea was a Japanese colony 1910-45.

manchuria.why: Manchuria's own state in the war years, Manchukuo (1932-1945).

formosa.why: A Japanese colony from 1895 to 1945, with no flag of its own in those years.

indochina.why: Vietnam's own flag, most of Indochina: first raised in the Cochinchina uprising against French rule in November 1940, the Viet Minh's from its founding in May 1941 (this form 1945-1955).

burma.why: Burma's own flag under the State of Burma (1943-45), with the green peacock, Burma's old national emblem. Before 1943 its only flag of its own was a British ensign.

malaya.why: The Federated Malay States' flag (1896-1942), the Malay rulers' federation.

dutch_east_indies.why: Indonesia's red and white: the national movement's flag from 1928, raised at the declaration of independence on 17 August 1945.

india.why: The Indian National Congress's flag from 1931, flown across India in the Quit India movement of 1942. British India's official flags were British ensigns.

ceylon.why: Ceylon's own lion flag: the Kingdom of Kandy's, replaced by the Union Flag at the British takeover in 1815 and restored at independence in 1948 (its 1948 form). Ceylon's only flag in between was a British ensign.

hawaii.why: Hawaii's own flag, the kingdom's since 1845, kept by the Territory of Hawaii.

midway.why: A United States possession, with no flag of its own.

wake_island.why: A United States possession, with no flag of its own.

marshall_islands.why: Japanese mandate islands, with no flag of their own until after the war.

marianas.why: Japanese mandate islands (Saipan, Tinian); Guam was taken from the United States in December 1941. No flag of their own until after the war.

gilbert_islands.why: The Gilbert and Ellice Islands' own flag (1937-1976), with its frigatebird badge.

new_guinea.why: The Territory of New Guinea's own flag.

solomon_islands.why: The British Solomon Islands Protectorate's own flag (1906-1947).

fiji.why: Fiji's own flag (1924-1970), with the colony's arms.

west_africa.why: French West Africa (Dakar), which had no flag of its own.

east_africa.why: Ethiopia's own flag: the system is Ethiopia (Addis Ababa), conquered by Italy in 1936 and freed in 1941.

madagascar.why: A French colony from 1896 to 1958, with no flag of its own in those years.
